problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=\sqrt{t}-{t}^{3/2}$, where $t>0$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=\frac{4}{15}\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=1\,\text{s}$, determine the moment in time when the particle is stationary.

activity_context.topic_title: Determining Characteristics of Moving Objects Using Integration

feedback.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}},$ where $t>0$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=1\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=9\,\text{s},$ determine the moment in time when the particle is stationary.
feedback.worked_solution:
The particle is stationary when $v=0\,\text{m}/\text{s}.$

First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int \frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\sqrt{t}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C,$ we use the fact that $v(9)=1.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =\sqrt{9}+C \\ 1 & =3+C \\ C & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=\sqrt{t}-2.$

Now, we find the moments in time when $v=0\,\text{m}/\text{s}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{t}-2 & =0 \\ \sqrt{t} & =2 \\ t & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the particle is stationary when $t=4\,\text{s}.$
